name: Smart Contract Tooling & Development Environment
description: The ecosystem of tools, frameworks, and services that make smart contract development productive and reliable. Covers crypto wallets for development (MetaMask, WalletConnect), IDEs and editor plugins, testnet faucets, decentralized storage (IPFS, Arweave, Filecoin), and the four major smart contract development frameworks (Hardhat, Brownie, Truffle, Foundry).

subskills.name: Crypto Wallets for Development
subskills.description: Using wallets as development and testing tools: MetaMask browser extension (custom RPC, test accounts, signing transactions in browser dApps), MetaMask Flask for experimental features (Snaps), WalletConnect v2 (QR-code wallet connection protocol for mobile wallets), Rainbow Kit and ConnectKit (React components for wallet connection UI), Hardhat Network accounts (deterministic test accounts from mnemonic), and cast wallet (Foundry's CLI wallet). Understanding the difference between signing a message and signing a transaction.

subskills.name: IDEs & Editor Tooling
subskills.description: Development environments for smart contract work: Remix IDE (browser-based, instant deployment, built-in debugger — ideal for prototyping), VS Code with solidity extension (Juan Blanco's extension: syntax highlighting, error detection, NatSpec hints), Cursor/GitHub Copilot for AI-assisted Solidity, Hardhat VSCode extension (inline test running), and Foundry toolchain integration. Remix's virtual machine, injected provider, and external provider modes.

subskills.name: Testnet Faucets
subskills.description: Services that distribute free testnet ETH or native tokens for development and testing: Sepolia faucets (Alchemy Faucet, QuickNode Faucet, Chainlink Faucet), Goerli/Holesky faucets, Mumbai/Amoy faucets for Polygon, Avalanche Fuji faucet, BSC testnet faucet, and Solana Devnet airdrop (solana airdrop command). Understanding testnet limitations vs mainnet, and why testnet state is reset or deprecated.

subskills.name: Decentralized Storage
subskills.description: Off-chain storage solutions for blockchain applications, essential for NFT metadata and large data that cannot live on-chain due to gas costs. IPFS (InterPlanetary File System): content-addressed storage using CID (content identifier), pinning services (Pinata, web3.storage, NFT.Storage), IPFS gateways. Arweave: permanent storage with one-time payment, Arweave permaweb, Bundlr/Irys for efficient uploads, AR token economics. Filecoin: incentivized IPFS storage with FIL token, storage deals, retrieval market. On-chain vs off-chain metadata trade-offs for NFT projects.

subskills.name: Hardhat
subskills.description: The most widely used Ethereum development framework (Node.js). Key features: Hardhat Network (local EVM with console.log in Solidity, stack traces, mining modes), task and plugin system (hardhat-ethers, hardhat-waffle, hardhat-etherscan, hardhat-gas-reporter, hardhat-coverage, OpenZeppelin hardhat-upgrades), compilation with solc version management, deployment scripts with hardhat-deploy, and fork testing (forking mainnet state). Configuration via hardhat.config.ts.

subskills.name: Foundry
subskills.description: Rust-based, fastest smart contract testing and development toolkit. Components: forge (compilation, testing, fuzzing, gas snapshots), cast (CLI for on-chain interactions — call, send, decode, estimate-gas, block), anvil (local EVM node with same features as Hardhat Network), chisel (REPL for Solidity). Foundry's Solidity-native test DSL (no JS wrapper), built-in fuzz testing (forge test --fuzz-runs), invariant testing, fork testing (--fork-url), and vm.prank, vm.deal, vm.expectRevert cheat codes.

subskills.name: Brownie
subskills.description: Python-based Ethereum development framework (now in maintenance mode, superseded largely by Foundry for many use cases). Key features: pytest integration for smart contract testing, Web3.py under the hood, accounts management, network management, contract interaction via Python objects, and console for interactive testing. Widely used in DeFi (Yearn Finance is built with Brownie). Relevant for teams with Python expertise or maintaining legacy codebases.

subskills.name: Truffle
subskills.description: One of the original Ethereum development frameworks (now in maintenance mode, superseded by Hardhat and Foundry). Historically significant: introduced the concept of migrations (sequential deployment scripts), Mocha/Chai testing, Ganache (local blockchain — now replaced by Hardhat Network/Anvil), and Truffle Boxes (project templates). Understanding Truffle is important for legacy codebase maintenance and understanding how migration patterns were established.

junior.description: Productive in Hardhat (or Foundry), uses MetaMask with custom RPC endpoints, obtains testnet tokens from faucets, and works in Remix or VS Code with Solidity extension.

mid.description: Proficient in Foundry's full toolchain (forge/cast/anvil), integrates IPFS or Arweave for NFT metadata and off-chain storage, and has used multiple frameworks.

senior.description: Navigates legacy Brownie/Truffle codebases, evaluates framework trade-offs for new projects, and contributes to toolchain decisions at the team or protocol level.
